s1.syndrome_frame: Acute kidney injury with proteinuria and hematuria in a patient with a left ventricular assist device
salient_findings: Increased serum creatinine from 124 μmol/L to 354 μmol/L over two months
Urinary protein excretion of 2.2 g/day with microhaematuria
Positive blood cultures for Corynebacterium jeikeium
key_facts: 55-year-old man with severe dilated cardiomyopathy
Left ventricular assist device (LVAD; HeartMate II) implanted four years previously
Admitted for evaluation of low-grade fever
Serum creatinine increased from 124 μmol/L to 354 μmol/L over two months
Urinary protein excretion of 2.2 g/day
Microhaematuria without dysmorphic erythrocytes or casts
Elevated C-reactive protein and procalcitonin
Low serum complement C3 concentrations
Elevated PR3-ANCA and rheumatoid factor concentrations
Negative anti-MPO-ANCA
Multiple foci of increased metabolic activity at the LVAD driveline insertion site, the ventricular assist device pocket, and the LVAD outflow cannula on 18F-FDG PET-CT

differentials: Chronic kidney disease with LVAD-associated nephropathy
per_call: Chronic kidney disease with LVAD-associated nephropathy

shortlist.label: Post-infectious glomerulonephritis
shortlist.why_kept: Patient has low-grade fever, elevated C-reactive protein and procalcitonin, and positive blood cultures for Corynebacterium jeikeium, which suggests a post-infectious cause for the glomerulonephritis

shortlist.label: C3 glomerulopathy
shortlist.why_kept: Renal biopsy shows positive mesangial staining for C3 and low serum complement C3 concentrations, which is consistent with C3 glomerulopathy

shortlist.label: Granulomatosis with polyangiitis
shortlist.why_kept: Elevated PR3-ANCA concentrations and renal biopsy findings of segmental necrotizing glomerulonephritis are consistent with granulomatosis with polyangiitis

shortlist.label: LVAD-associated infection with Corynebacterium jeikeium
shortlist.why_kept: Patient has a left ventricular assist device and positive blood cultures for Corynebacterium jeikeium, which suggests a device-related infection

shortlist.label: Antineutrophil cytoplasmic antibody-associated vasculitis
shortlist.why_kept: Elevated PR3-ANCA concentrations and renal biopsy findings of segmental necrotizing glomerulonephritis are consistent with antineutrophil cytoplasmic antibody-associated vasculitis

raw.rationale: The presence of elevated PR3-ANCA concentrations, which are specific for Granulomatosis with polyangiitis (GPA), along with renal involvement indicated by proteinuria, microhaematuria, and the findings on renal biopsy, supports this diagnosis. The patient's systemic symptoms such as low-grade fever and elevated inflammatory markers also align with GPA.

rejected.label: Post-infectious glomerulonephritis
rejected.why: While the patient has an infection with Corynebacterium jeikeium, the presence of PR3-ANCA and the specific renal biopsy findings are more indicative of an autoimmune process like GPA rather than a post-infectious glomerulonephritis.

rejected.label: C3 glomerulopathy
rejected.why: Although the patient has low serum complement C3 concentrations and positive mesangial staining for C3, the clinical context and the presence of PR3-ANCA point more towards GPA.

rejected.label: LVAD-associated infection with Corynebacterium jeikeium
rejected.why: While the patient does have an LVAD and an infection, the systemic nature of the illness including renal involvement and the presence of ANCA suggest a more complex autoimmune process.

rejected.label: Antineutrophil cytoplasmic antibody-associated vasculitis
rejected.why: This is a broader category that includes GPA. Given the specific findings, GPA is a more precise diagnosis within this category.
